learning_outcomes.text: Students have developed the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Improved written and oral communicative competence (obj. 2)
Adaptation to different levels of formality (obj. 2)
Understand language at a deeper level to find the best resources (obj. 3)
Greater linguistic awareness to communicate beyond mere language transmission, at a professional and academic level (obj. 3)

syllabus_topics: Vowels: long, short, diphthongs, the importance of the schwa vowel
Phonological and speech processes: pronunciation of -ed verbs, elision of /d/ and /h/ sounds, words ending in 's', connected speech, linking phonemes, silent letters, phoneme coalescence
Other phenomena: weak and strong forms, stress in compound and simple words
teaching_methods: Lectures focused on presenting and explaining content and material, and completing activities
Seminars dedicated to planning assessment tasks, rehearsing presentations, practicing pronunciation, developing writing, and resolving doubts
assessment_rules: The default assessment system is continuous assessment. For continuous assessment, students must deliver or complete a series of tasks, a short exam, and a presentation, and all tasks must be passed to be included in the final grade. Active participation is mandatory and accounts for 10% of the global grade. Students not following continuous assessment must formally waive it, otherwise the ordinary call may be failed. Final assessment requires students to prepare content and develop competencies independently, passing all 5 parts of the final exam in one attempt; failing one part results in failing the subject. The extraordinary exam is for students who did not pass continuous assessment or the ordinary exam, and also comprises 5 independent sections that must all be passed.
